clue.text: see 24dn.
Do not sit around for a facetious oral prober

indicators.note: letters moved around are no longer in their original order, so the phrase is rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction not to sit around, as if waiting at the dentist's.
explanation.definitionFit: Odontist is a jocular, mock-learned word for a dentist, someone who probes your mouth.

clue.text: (& 8dn/26ac.) UK piss artist? One of many in the House

definitions.meaning: jokey reading: a 'pee-er' (one who pisses) belonging to the ..., i.e. the UK

definitions.text: One of many in the House
definitions.meaning: straight reading: a member of the House of Lords

explanation.surface: A drunk in Britain is likened to the many members of Parliament's upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss artist is British slang for a drunk; here it is read literally as someone who pees, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a hereditary or life noble entitled to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Bury originally named Archer once

parts.note: née marks the name someone was born with

explanation.surface: The Lancashire town of Bury is said to have first named someone called Archer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed for perjury in 2001, so he was once held in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined or detained, as Archer was during his prison term.

clue.text: I'm awash with lust — could well turn 29, or the political opposite

definitions.text: could well turn 29, or the political opposite
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun: what the answer does

indicators.note: something awash is sloshing about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone overwhelmed by desire could swing to the Tory side or to Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is TRUE BLUE; litmus turns blue in alkali and red in acid, and blue and red are the Tory and Labour colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is the indicator dye that changes colour to blue or red depending on acidity.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Fancy Desmond Tutu's capital leftovers

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into an ornate new order
a capital letter is the first one, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: first letter of the archbishop's surname

explanation.surface: Archbishop Desmond Tutu's spare cash, or what is left of his capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are odd remaining pieces, scraps left over from something larger.

clue.text: see3dn.
Standard feature of Ken's ignorance

indicators.note: a feature is part of something, so the word sits inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: runs across the apostrophe and into the next word

explanation.surface: Ignorance is a regular trait of someone called Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and an ensign is a flag flown to show nationality.

clue.text: Flag-waving gets Jack elected: "Bash insipid socialist and multiracialist leaders!"

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
have a bash means have a go

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so each of these words gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the initials of these three words; 'and' is passed over

explanation.surface: A jingoistic campaign slogan attacking dull left-wingers and champions of a mixed society.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoism is aggressive patriotism, whose outward show is waving the national flag.

clue.text: Obama's moral integrity (or nearest offer when pressed by hard right)

indicators.note: something pressed on both sides is squeezed between two things

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dig at a President's principles being up for haggling under pressure from conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obama's' tells you to use the American spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Honor is the US spelling of honour, meaning moral uprightness and integrity.

clue.text: Skinny thing simpered playfully — Cyclops ensnarled

indicators.note: something ensnarled is caught up inside a tangle, so it goes within the jumble
doing something playfully means messing about with it, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: the setter Cyclops refers to himself, so I

explanation.surface: A thin creature gave a coy smile and got the setter tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' is not slim here but 'made of skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outermost layer of skin, so it is literally a skin-like thing.

clue.text: Binge drinkers will have this bad, squeezing tip of dick

indicators.note: squeezing something means holding it tightly within, so one piece goes inside the other
the tip is an extremity, here the final letter of the word

parts.note: the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crude remark about heavy drinkers and their sexual health.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is British slang for enough alcohol to make you drunk, the goal of a binge.

clue.text: House just about wants Hague's head in fire

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so the first letter of the name

parts.note: first letter of the Tory politician's name

explanation.surface: A political call that William Hague should face the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A shack is a crude hut, a dwelling that barely qualifies as a house.

clue.text: Being a student, inclined to imbibe very last trace of beer

indicators.note: imbibing means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
the very last trace is the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Student life: a tendency to down the dregs of the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is engaged in learning, the process of acquiring knowledge through study.

clue.text: Group seeing off Sting's opener

indicators.note: something off is out of kilter or wrong, so the letters are put in a different order
an opener comes first, so only the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: first letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: A rock band defeats the singer Sting's support act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing off' reads as one phrase meaning defeating, but 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is a famous English rock band, an example of a musical group.

clue.text: Come, it could protect many such swimmers

definitions.note: loose slang: the fluid named by the cells it carries

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the male cells that swim, which semen holds and protects

explanation.surface: An invitation to someone whose role is to keep lots of swimmers safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words tie the two meanings together: semen contains and protects millions of the swimming cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm is used both for seminal fluid and for the spermatozoa, tiny cells that swim with a tail.

clue.text: The lost cause of Clegg's veto, as Cyclops might cryptically put it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Nick Clegg's electoral reform, defeated in the 2011 referendum

definitions.text: veto, as Cyclops might cryptically put it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: veto is a rearranged 'vote', and setters flag rearrangements with words like 'alternative'

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg's failed cause and his supposed veto, described the way the setter would clue it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2011 UK referendum the Lib Dem leader's preferred voting reform was rejected; the second half is a joke about how a crossword setter would describe the word veto.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alternative Vote is a preferential voting system rejected in the 2011 UK referendum that Clegg had championed.

clue.text: Bantering, creative stuff, with judge's bottom grasped by depraved peer

indicators.note: something grasped is held within another's hands
depraved means corrupted, so the word is twisted out of shape
the bottom of a down word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Witty creative material about a judge's backside being groped by a corrupt lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty exchange of remarks, the activity of trading banter.

clue.text: Not even crap will do for whackos

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
balls is British slang for nonsense, as is crap

explanation.surface: Lousy material that is not quite level will satisfy eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddballs and whackos are both slang for eccentric or crazy people.

clue.text: Key figure in government initially, wearing naff pink

indicators.note: the one wearing a garment surrounds the thing worn
naff means shoddy or badly made, so the word is put together wrongly
initially points at the first letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: An important government figure dressed in tacky pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in an organisation, the one everything depends on.

clue.text: Not so sensitive '69'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more numb, the comparative of numb, read with a silent b
second meaning: sixty-nine is an example of a figure, flagged by the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 69 nudge towards the sex position, but it is just an integer; the first sense is pronounced NUM-er, comparative of numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means lacking feeling, so its comparative means less feeling; and 69 is simply an integer.

clue.text: Brothel-keeper shafted by Bill and stuff in the road

explanation.surface: A brothel owner done over by somebody called Bill, with stuff littering the street.

clue.text: Holy shit tax once used to keep a corporation in check

definitions.text: used to keep a corporation in check

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
Selective Employment Tax, a UK payroll tax from 1966 to 1973

explanation.surface: Outrage at an old tax applied to rein in a big company.

clue.text: Notes Major at first (having screwed Norma and Edwina): "No win!"

explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes or reminders, the plural of memorandum.

clue.text: (& 1/6/27) Organise a get-together of a couple of arses to avoid a debt crisis?

definitions.text: Organise a get-together of a couple of arses
definitions.meaning: jokey literal meaning: cause two backsides to come together
idiomatic meaning: to manage financially on what you earn

explanation.walkthrough: An arse is a rear end, so two of them are both ends; the question mark flags the idiom being taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means earning just enough to cover your expenses, so you stay out of debt.

clue.text: Hot as the stuff of politicians' speeches?

definitions.text: Hot as the stuff of politicians' speeches?

parts.words: Hot as the stuff of politicians' speeches?
parts.note: surface reading: speeches that are fiery, heated

parts.words: Hot as the stuff of politicians' speeches?
parts.note: cryptic reading: the word that follows 'hot' in the phrase for empty talk

explanation.walkthrough: Put 'hot' in front of the answer to get the stock phrase for empty, boastful talk.

clue.text: Right miserable as a constant supporter of Cameron & co.
